#Problem 1
### To import data and clean names
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

Subway_df = 
  read.csv("./data/NYC_Transit_Subway_Entrance_And_Exit_Data.csv")

Subway_df = 
  janitor::clean_names(Subway_df)

```

### Then read and clean the data; retain line, station, name, station latitude / longitude, routes served, entry, vending, entrance type, and ADA compliance.

```{r}
Subway_df =
  Subway_df |>
  select(
    line,
    station_name,
    station_latitude,
    station_longitude,
    route1:route11,
    entry,
    vending,
    entrance_type,
    ada
  ) |>
  mutate(
    entry = case_match(
      entry,
      "YES" ~ TRUE,
      "NO" ~ FALSE
    )
  )

dim(Subway_df)


```
Now this dataset contains subway line and station name, station latitude/ longitude, routes served, entry status, vending availability, entrance type, and ADA. I cleaned the variable names using janitor::clean_names(), selected the variables relevant to this analysis, and converted the entry variable from "YES" and "NO" character values to a logical variable. The resulting dataset has 1868 rows and 19 columns. The data are not fully tidy because route information is spread across route1 to route11 instead of being stored in one variable.



```{r}
###How many distinct stations?
Subway_df |>
  distinct(line, station_name) |>
  nrow()

###How many stations are ADA compliant?

Subway_df |>
  filter(ada == TRUE) |>
  distinct(line, station_name) |>
  nrow()

###What proportion of station entrances / exits without vending allow entrance?
Subway_df |>
  filter(vending == "NO") |>
  summarize(
    proportion = mean(entry)
  )

### How many distinct stations serve the A train? and how many are ADA compliant?
Subway_long =
  Subway_df |>
  mutate(
    across(route1:route11, as.character)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    route1:route11,
    names_to = "route_number",
    values_to = "route_name"
  )

Subway_long |>
  filter(route_name == "A") |>
  distinct(line, station_name) |>
  nrow()

Subway_long |>
  filter(route_name == "A", ada == TRUE) |>
  distinct(line, station_name) |>
  nrow()
```

# Question 2
### specify the sheet in the Excel file and to omit non-data entries (rows with notes / figures; columns containing notes) using arguments in read_excel

```{r}
trash_df = 
  readxl::read_excel("./data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx",
    sheet = "Mr. Trash Wheel",
    range = "A2:N549"
  ) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  drop_na(dumpster) |>
  mutate(
    sports_balls = as.integer(round(sports_balls))
  )


```


### To combine data from from Mr. Trash Wheel, Professor Trash Wheel , and Gwynnda



```{r}
trash_path = "data/202610 Trash Wheel Collection Data.xlsx"

# Mr. Trash Wheel
mr_trash_df =
  readxl::read_excel(
    trash_path,
    sheet = "Mr. Trash Wheel",
    range = readxl::cell_limits(
      c(2, 1),
      c(NA, 14)
    ),
    na = c("", "NA", "dive")
  ) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  tidyr::drop_na(dumpster) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dumpster = as.integer(dumpster),
    month = stringr::str_to_title(
      stringr::str_trim(month)
    ),
    year = as.integer(year),
    sports_balls =
      as.integer(round(sports_balls)),
    trash_wheel = "Mr. Trash Wheel"
  )


# Professor Trash Wheel
professor_trash_df =
  readxl::read_excel(
    trash_path,
    sheet = "Professor Trash Wheel",
    range = readxl::cell_limits(
      c(2, 1),
      c(NA, 13)
    ),
    na = c("", "NA", "dive")
  ) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  tidyr::drop_na(dumpster) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dumpster = as.integer(dumpster),
    month = stringr::str_to_title(
      stringr::str_trim(month)
    ),
    year = as.integer(year),
    trash_wheel = "Professor Trash Wheel"
  )


# Gwynnda
gwynnda_df =
  readxl::read_excel(
    trash_path,
    sheet = "Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the W",
    range = readxl::cell_limits(
      c(2, 1),
      c(NA, 12)
    ),
    na = c("", "NA", "dive")
  ) |>
  janitor::clean_names() |>
  tidyr::drop_na(dumpster) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dumpster = as.integer(dumpster),
    month = stringr::str_to_title(
      stringr::str_trim(month)
    ),
    year = as.integer(year),
    trash_wheel = "Gwynnda"
  )

trash_df =
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    mr_trash_df,
    professor_trash_df,
    gwynnda_df
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    trash_wheel,
    everything()
  )

dim(trash_df)
names(trash_df)
```
###To Calculate the weight: 

```{r}
professor_df =
  trash_df |>
  filter(
    trash_wheel == "Professor Trash Wheel"
  )
```
